title: SRE documentation: SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, Reliability Initiatives and Runbooks
author: Ari Chen
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference











’s SRE documentation standards for SLOs and error budgets, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, incident review standards, operational tooling, and runbooks. It is intended as the canonical reference used by SRE, serving-runtime, and platform teams when defining, operating, and improving service reliability.

Scope

- Applies to all customer-facing inference services (hosted API, dedicated runtime, private control plane) and critical internal services supporting them (scheduler, KV cache, routing layer, telemetry ingestion).
- Documents the lifecycle: definition -> measurement -> alerting -> incident response -> post-incident review -> improvement.

1) SLO taxonomy and definition

Purpose: SLOs express reliability expectations in measurable terms and drive error-budget-driven decisions.

SLO levels (recommended):
- Platinum (customer-facing SLA-backed paths): availability 99.95% (monthly), p99 latency target 150 ms for short responses
- Gold (high-traffic model endpoints): availability 99.9% (monthly), p99 latency target 250 ms
- Standard (background or non-critical APIs): availability 99.5% (monthly), p99 latency target 500 ms

SLO components (required in every SLO doc):
- target: numeric percentage or latency percentile
- measurement window: rolling 30d (default) or 90d for long-lived contracts
- KPI and signal: e.g., successful_response_rate computed from nginx-proxy 2xx/3xx and model-serving OK status; or inference_latency_ms measured at ingress after queuing
- owner: team + primary oncall
- error budget: 1 - target over window and alert thresholds (see next section)

Example SLO: Hosted Text-Generation Ingress
- target: 99.9% successful_response_rate per 30-day rolling window
- signal: metric inference.request.success{route="text-generate"} / inference.request.total
- objective window: 30d rolling
- owner: eng-serving-runtime (oncall: inference-sre)
- error budget: 0.1% monthly burn allowed

2) Error budget policy and burn management

Principles:
- Error budget is the mechanism to balance reliability vs. feature velocity. When the budget is healthy teams may proceed with rollouts; when depleted, mitigations / rollout freezes occur.
- Burn should be computed from the same signal used in the SLO.

Burn thresholds and actions (default policy):
- Green (<=25% of monthly error budget consumed): normal operations and regular rollouts allowed.
- Yellow (25% - 60% consumed): increased review for large rollouts; require SRE sign-off for risky changes.
- Red (60% - 100% consumed): hold non-critical rollouts; perform blameless review and run mitigations.
- Exhausted (>100%): immediate action: notify product and execs, escalate to incident response if degradation ongoing.

Alerting on burn rate:
- Alert when 30d burn rate suggests budget will be exhausted within 48 hours (pager alert to SRE), and when 7d burn exceeds 75% (email + Slack channel).

3) Capacity planning process

Objective: ensure predictable capacity for latency/throughput SLOs across burst and steady-state traffic.

Key artifacts (per service):
- Capacity plan document (updated quarterly) with traffic forecasts, HW pool sizing, and autoscaling policies.
- Traffic model: QPS peaks, 95/99 percentile request size, KV cache hit rates, cold-start frequency.
- Failure modes: degraded autoscale, GPU OOMs, networking congestion.

Capacity table (example):
| Metric | Baseline | Headroom | Target pool | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Peak QPS (30d p99) | 12,000 | +40% | 100 x A100 | supports 3ms mean inference kernel |
| Avg GPU memory usage | 72% | +10% | 100 x A100 | set reserve to avoid OOMs on quantized models |
| Cache hit rate | 62% | +15% | N/A | improve via prefix caching suggestions |

Quarterly capacity planning checklist:
1. Update traffic forecast and compare to current pool utilization.
2. Run canary traffic simulation (staging) for proposed autoscale changes.
3. Validate model variants and quantization profiles under new load.
4. Schedule capacity purchases or cloud reservations at 60 days lead time if forecasted growth > 30%.

Autoscaling guardrails:
- Minimum reserve: 15% of pool for burst buffer for Platinum services.
- Scale-down cooldown: 10 minutes to avoid oscillations.
- Maximum single-step scale-up: 3x to prevent noisy neighbor amplification.

4) Reliability initiatives and prioritization

Initiative intake process:
- Proposals submitted to reliability backlog with problem statement, hypothesis, success metrics (SLO improvement, cost reduction, MTTR).
- SRE triage board prioritizes by customer impact and ROI.

Typical initiative types:
- Observability gaps (tracing coverage, missing metrics)
- Performance (kernel selection, batching improvements)
- Cost & efficiency (better batching, model quantization)
- Resilience (fallbacks, circuit breakers, canary automation)

Example initiative: KV cache TTL tuning
- Problem: low cache hit rate causes higher model invocations and cost spikes
- Hypothesis: increasing TTL and adding LRU tuning will improve hit rate by 12% and reduce p95 latency by 8%
- Success criteria: +10% hit rate sustained for 14d, reduce cost per inference by 6%
- Owner: eng-serving-runtime + infra SRE

5) Incident review standards (postmortem hygiene)

Goals: produce blameless, actionable postmortems that capture timeline, impact, root cause, and permanent mitigations.

Required postmortem sections:
- Title and incident ID
- Summary (1-2 sentences)
- Severity (sev1/sev2/sev3) and impact (customers affected, revenue, feature availability)
- Timeline (UTC timestamps, short bullets)
- Root cause analysis (technical and organizational contributing factors)
- Actions (immediate and long-term), owners, deadlines
- Error budget impact and follow-up review date
- Lessons learned and playbook updates required

Postmortem SLAs:
- Initial incident review (bridge summary) within 4 hours of detection (Slack + incident tracker).
- Draft postmortem published within 72 hours.
- Final postmortem with assigned action items within 14 days.

Severity definitions (guidance):
- Sev1: customer-visible outage affecting >5% of traffic or SLA breach. Pager to oncall, exec notification required.
- Sev2: significant degradation (latency, errors) affecting a subset of customers or non-SLA paths. Pager to team oncall.
- Sev3: minor impact, internal only, no pager by default.

6) Operational tooling and observability standards

Required telemetry and ownership:
- Metrics: request rate, success rate, latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99/p999), queue depth, GPU utilization, cache hit rate.
- Traces: end-to-end traces from ingress SDK through scheduler to model host (sampling policy: 100% for errors, 1% baseline, 10% for canaries).
- Logs: structured JSON logs with request_id, route, model_version, tenant_id where applicable.

Alerting standards:
- Alert fatigue avoidance: prefer aggregated alerts and dynamic thresholds. Use paging only for signals tied to SLOs or critical infrastructure failure.
- Firing conditions should include context (last 15m trend, impacted services).

Operational runbook registry:
- All critical runbooks must be checked into the runbook registry (owner, last_tested date, steps, rollback actions). Quarterly runbook tests are required and logged.

Tooling inventory (canonical):
- Metrics: Prometheus + Cortex (long-term), Grafana for dashboards
- Tracing: Jaeger + OTEL collector
- Logs: Loki + Kibana
- Incident management: PagerDuty + Incident Tracker (confluence postmortem templates)
- Chaos and load testing: K6 + internal traffic replay service

7) SRE runbook template and example

Runbook metadata (required fields):
- runbook_id: short slug (e.g., inference-high-latency)
- owner: team and primary oncall
- last_tested: YYYY-MM-DD
- severity: sev1|sev2|sev3

Runbook: inference-high-latency
- Owner: eng-serving-runtime (oncall: inference-sre)
- Last tested: 2028-02-20
- Severity: sev2

Symptoms:
- p99 inference latency > 500 ms sustained for 10 minutes
- Increase in queue depth and GPU utilization > 90%
- Error rate trending up (5xx) for model-serving host group

Immediate actions (1st 10 minutes):
1. Acknowledge pager and join the dedicated incident channel.
2. Run quick health checks: curl /health on router, scheduler, model-hosts (prefer scripted checks: ./tools/health-check --service inference)
3. Verify recent deployments (git/CI) and rolling windows: last 30m deploys to model-hosts or router.
4. If queue depth > threshold, temporarily increase autoscale target by +25% (use autoscale playbook CLI: infra autoscale set --pool inference --factor 1.25) and add capacity from burst pool.
5. If a recent model rollout correlates with latency increase, perform immediate rollback to previous model_version via rollout service: rdo rollback --service inference --to-tag stable --fast

Troubleshooting checklist (next 30 minutes):
- Inspect traces for slow spans (router, scheduling, model-inference).
- Check GPU metrics: memory usage, SM utilization, kernel stalls.
- Validate cache hit rates; if hit rate dropped, consider disabling cache eviction policy or extending TTL as temporary mitigation.
- If errors indicate out-of-memory or OOM kills, reduce concurrent per-GPU tokens or change batching policy.

Mitigations and follow-up:
- Restore service to SLO within 60 minutes via rollback or scale-up.
- Open postmortem template and populate timeline and root cause. Assign owners for permanent fixes (e.g., kernel fallback, autoscale tuning).
- Update runbook with new checks and thresholds after mitigation completed.

8) Governance and review cadence

- Weekly SRE triage: quick review of active error budgets, ongoing incidents, and hot reliability initiative blockers.
- Monthly reliability review: deep-dive on SLO health, capacity forecasts, and progress on initiatives. Include product and infra stakeholders.
- Quarterly runbook tabletop exercises: test at least two critical runbooks per quarter with SRE and product participants.

Appendix: Useful commands and links

- Health checks: ./tools/health-check --service inference
- Rollout status: rdo status --service inference
- Autoscale CLI: infra autoscale set --pool inference --factor 1.25
- Postmortem template: /confluence/eng-sre/templates/postmortem-template.json
- Runbook registry: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/index.json

Ownership and contacts

- Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime (oncall alias: inference-sre@pagerduty.com)
- Secondary owner: eng-platform (oncall alias: infra-sre@pagerduty.com)
- Exec escalation: eng-ops-lead@redwood.ai
